notes: the ONLY type in this matrix where AUTO reaches the canonical layer -- because there is no identity/link decision being made

input_example: a phrase with no clear source attribution
gate_reason: provenance gap does not block computation, only limits future attribution
notes: still auto -- weak provenance is a data-quality flag, not a merge/identity risk

gate_reason: ambiguous target -- machine cannot pick which Hebrew word is meant, per Sec.5 no similarity-only decisions
notes: a real failure mode this matrix must cover even without a live example on hand

duplicate_check_result: all 3 already exist independently, unrelated meanings
auto_ceiling: terminal at validated_candidate -- but NEVER escalated to Zuriel as a link request (Sec.4: E never proceeds to [10])

scenario: כהן <-> priest (shared_value, NOT translation, per live data)
computation_rule: Hebrew side computed (רגיל=75); English side skipped
auto_ceiling: n/a -- already exists, already human_verified=true on record
target_mechanism_on_approval: language_bridge node, relationship_type=shared_value (kept distinct from translation)
human_gate_required: NO -- already resolved/verified in live data
gate_reason: the live system already correctly classifies this as a numeric coincidence with a human-curated concept-seed, not an identity/translation claim -- and a human already verified that classification
notes: shows type E is not "wrong" or "less real" -- כהן/priest genuinely share meaning AND the model still correctly labels the specific claim on record as shared_value/English-Ordinal rather than translation, because that IS the method a human actually verified

input_example: "דוד המלך" proposed as an expansion of "דוד"
computation_rule: both live-computed, DIFFERENT values as expected (title adds letters)
auto_ceiling: the LONGER PHRASE ITSELF may reach gematria_words via the type-A path (no relation claim needed for that alone); the IDENTITY-RELATION to "דוד" is HELD at idea/discussion
zuriel_required_for_canonical_write: NO for registering the phrase itself (type-A path); YES, always, for the identity-relation
target_mechanism_on_approval: gematria_words insert for the longer phrase (may already be automatic); identity-relation link is a SEPARATE Zuriel-only proposal
human_gate_required: NO for phrase registration; YES for the identity-relation
gate_reason: Sec.9: identity merge always requires a human -- a title/expansion is not automatically "the same entity" for gematria purposes, even though the phrase itself can register independently
notes: see Spec Sec.10.1s sibling case -- proves identity != spelling != gematria one more time (14, then 109, for one referent under two names)

scenario: כהן -> מלך המשיח (title far exceeding a simple name, weak same-referent claim)
input_example: a compound royal-messianic title proposed as "the same as" a bare word
duplicate_check_result: both exist independently, ragil very different (75 vs 453)
auto_ceiling: no relation is even proposed -- falls back to two independent type-A registrations
zuriel_required_for_canonical_write: N/A -- no relation claim exists to gate
target_mechanism_on_approval: gematria_words insert for each phrase independently -- NO relation proposed
human_gate_required: N/A -- the machine does not even propose a relation here
gate_reason: too large a semantic gap between "priest" and "King Messiah" for the machine to propose F at all -- correctly falls back to two independent type-A inserts
notes: illustrates the boundary of type F: it applies to genuine title-expansions of the SAME name-root (דוד -> דוד המלך), not to loosely-related titles

input_example: the same Hebrew phrase submitted twice
computation_rule: not re-run -- existing gematria_words values reused
target_mechanism_on_approval: no new record -- routed to the existing gematria_words row
gate_reason: not a candidate at all, per gematria_auto_registry_laws own dedup-by-phrase rule
notes: step [2] terminates the pipeline immediately -- this is intentional, not an edge case to design around

scenario: Two intake mechanisms independently claim the same relation (the live סוד/Secret case)
input_example: word_aliases AND language_bridge both record a Hebrew<->English link for the same word, inconsistently
proposed_type: D or E (contested between the two existing records)
duplicate_check_result: COLLISION across mechanisms, not caught by either mechanisms own duplicate check
auto_ceiling: HELD -- cannot pre-validate a cross-mechanism collision
gate_reason: Sec.9 translation vs shared_value ambiguity, PLUS this reveals step [2] must check BOTH word_aliases and language_bridge, not just one, for any candidate touching a word that could plausibly have either
notes: the single most important design lesson from live data -- step [2] of the state machine is written to close exactly this gap going forward

scenario: Non-Hebrew candidate with NO Hebrew counterpart proposed
input_example: a foreign word submitted with no claimed Hebrew relationship at all
proposed_type: none of A-F -- out of scope for this intake path
computation_rule: no computation possible or meaningful without a Hebrew anchor
zuriel_required_for_canonical_write: N/A -- would need its own future design, not covered here
target_mechanism_on_approval: not inserted via this pipeline -- would need its own foreign_word-only node, if ever wanted, as a separate future design question
gate_reason: this specs state machine assumes every candidate ultimately anchors to a Hebrew identity -- a foreign word with no Hebrew link is outside what word_aliases/language_bridge are built to hold today
notes: disclosed boundary of this design, not silently absorbed
